policies.hint: Adjust system-wide defaults. Items marked "Module override" can be set separately on the module design page. Tightening a limit only affects new additions; existing data is left alone.

maxRulesPerModule.name: Task rules per module limit
maxRulesPerModule.help: No new rules can be added beyond this; existing rules can still be edited.

maxTasksPerRule.help: When editing an existing rule, the limit is only checked if the number of tasks increases.

reminderLeadDays.name: Remind within this many days before due
reminderLeadDays.help: Within this many days before the due date (including the due date itself), the assignee gets one "due soon" notification. Each task is reminded only once; changing the due date or assignee starts over.

remindOverdue.name: Remind when overdue
remindOverdue.help: When on, the assignee gets at most one reminder a day about an unfinished overdue task; no new one is added while the previous one is unread.

commented.name: Who is notified of a new comment
commented.help: A mentioned person gets "mentioned you" instead, never both. The commenter is not notified.

completed.name: Who is notified when a task is completed
completed.help: The person who completed it is not notified. Tasks created by the system have no creator.

cancelled.name: Who is notified when a task is cancelled
cancelled.help: The person who cancelled it is not notified. Tasks created by the system have no creator.

subtasksDone.name: Who is notified when all subtasks are done or cancelled
subtasksDone.help: Goes to the parent task's assignee or creator. The person who closed the last subtask is not notified, and nothing is sent when every subtask was cancelled.

supervisorScope.name: Managers see and reassign subordinates' tasks
supervisorScope.help: When on, a department manager sees tasks assigned to subordinates (or unassigned tasks created by a subordinate) and can reassign the assignee; other fields stay read-only.

supervisorScopeRecursive.name: Manager scope includes child departments
supervisorScopeRecursive.help: When on, subordinates include members of child departments; when off, only the departments the manager directly manages count.

maxSubtasksPerTask.name: Subtasks per task limit
maxSubtasksPerTask.help: Completed and cancelled subtasks count. Lowering the limit only blocks new subtasks; existing ones are not affected.

retentionDays.name: Notification retention (days)
retentionDays.help: After shortening, older notifications are removed by the background schedule or the next time notifications are opened.

reminderScanMinutes.name: Background reminder and cleanup interval (minutes)
reminderScanMinutes.help: While the system is running, every this many minutes it adds due reminders for everyone and removes notifications older than the retention period. A change takes effect from the next scheduled run.

weekStart.name: First day of the week
weekStart.help: Affects the "due this week" filter, and this week, last week and last N weeks in reports and dashboards.

maxFileBytes.name: Maximum file size (bytes)
maxFileBytes.help: 10485760 bytes is 10 MB; larger files cannot be uploaded.

maxFilesPerField.name: Files per attachment field limit
maxFilesPerField.help: Records already over the limit can still be viewed and have files removed, but no more can be uploaded.

allowedExtensions.name: Allowed file extensions
allowedExtensions.help: Anything not listed is rejected on upload; shrinking the list does not affect files already uploaded. Web pages, scripts and executables (such as html, svg, js, exe) are never accepted for security and cannot be added.

maxFilesPerComment.name: Attachments per comment limit
maxFilesPerComment.help: The most files one comment can carry at once.

slowRequestMs.name: Slow request threshold (ms)
slowRequestMs.help: Requests slower than this are logged as a warning. Changes take effect within 60 seconds.

clientErrorCollection.name: Collect front-end errors
clientErrorCollection.help: When on, program errors that occur on users' screens are written to the system log for administrators and the vendor to investigate. An error message may include a small amount of text shown on screen, so treat the log as sensitive data. Changes take effect within 60 seconds.

upkeepMinutes.name: Ops upkeep interval (minutes)
upkeepMinutes.help: Every this many minutes the system runs ops upkeep, such as removing audit records older than the retention period. A change takes effect from the next scheduled run.

auditRetentionDays.name: Audit record retention (days)
auditRetentionDays.help: Audit records (sign-ins, administration and design changes) are kept for this many days; older records are removed in batches by the background schedule.

monitorScanMinutes.name: Ops monitor interval (minutes)
monitorScanMinutes.help: Every this many minutes the system sends pending alert emails and runs scheduled health checks that are due. A change takes effect from the next scheduled run.

healthResultRetentionDays.name: Health check and alert email record retention (days)
healthResultRetentionDays.help: Each health check result and the records of finished alert emails are kept for this many days; older ones are removed in batches by the background schedule.

incidentRetentionDays.name: Resolved ops incident retention (days)
incidentRetentionDays.help: Resolved ops incidents are kept for this many days after they are resolved, then removed together with their samples. If the same problem occurs again afterwards, it becomes a new incident.

incidentSampleRetentionDays.name: Incident raw sample retention (days)
incidentSampleRetentionDays.help: Raw messages and stack traces of server exceptions and front-end errors may contain record content, so they are kept only this many days. The incident itself follows the incident retention.

incidentRenotifyHours.name: Critical incident reminder interval (hours)
incidentRenotifyHours.help: While nobody has acknowledged a critical incident, a reminder is sent again every this many hours.

incidentAutoResolveHours.name: Incident auto-resolve (hours)
incidentAutoResolveHours.help: Product defect, configuration error and security incidents are resolved automatically when they have not occurred again for this many hours.

alertRecipients.name: Ops incident notification recipients
alertRecipients.help: Who receives in-app notifications for infrastructure, product defect and security incidents. If everyone listed is deactivated, all system administrators are notified instead.

alertEmailCategories.name: Incident categories that send alert emails
alertEmailCategories.help: For the selected categories, a new, regressed, escalated, or re-notified incident also sends an email to the addresses in the alert channel settings, in addition to the in-app notification. Select none to never send email. Customer configuration incidents are in-app only by default, for the designer who owns the rule.

alertEmailMinSeverity.name: Minimum severity for alert emails
alertEmailMinSeverity.help: Incidents below this severity only send in-app notifications, not email.

alertEmailMaxPerHour.name: Maximum alert emails per hour
alertEmailMaxPerHour.help: Once this many emails have been sent within an hour, further alerts are not sent one by one; they are combined into one digest email at the next hour. The digest itself is not limited.

loginFailureWindowMinutes.name: Sign-in failure counting window (minutes)
loginFailureWindowMinutes.help: The sign-in failures health check counts the failed sign-ins within this many minutes.

schedulerLagIntervals.name: Scheduler lag intervals before critical
schedulerLagIntervals.help: When the next run of any scheduled job is late by more than this many intervals, the scheduler health check is critical (the scheduler is stuck or cannot get its lease).

rulePauseConsecutiveFailures.name: Consecutive failures before a task rule is paused
rulePauseConsecutiveFailures.help: When the same task rule fails this many times in a row within the time window below (with no success in between), it is paused automatically: saving records still works, but the rule creates no tasks until someone resumes it. A new value applies from the next failure.

rulePauseWindowMinutes.name: Time window for consecutive failures
rulePauseWindowMinutes.help: On each failure, the system looks back this many minutes; if the failures since the last success reach the limit, the rule is paused. After enlarging the window, failures already outside the old window are not counted again.

configIssueRecipients.name: Who is notified of rule problems
configIssueRecipients.help: Who receives in-app notifications when a task rule is paused automatically, or when an event or check fails because of its settings. You can choose "the rule's last editor". If everyone listed is deactivated, all system administrators are notified instead.

maxStages.name: Maximum stages per flow
maxStages.help: Lowering it only affects flows added or edited afterwards. Saved flows keep working, and saving one unchanged is not blocked.

maxBranches.name: Maximum branches per fork node
maxBranches.help: The most parallel branches a single fork node can have in a flow graph. Lowering it only affects flows added or edited afterwards. Saved flows keep working, and saving one unchanged is not blocked.

maxApprovers.name: Maximum approvers per stage
maxApprovers.help: When saving a flow, lowering this only blocks what is newly added or increased; a saved flow can be saved again unchanged. At run time, the stage's own source (groups, managers, user fields and the people the submitter picks) is checked against the current setting when each stage starts, and an approval action returns 409 when it is exceeded (submitter picks use the smaller of the saved maximum and the current setting); a stage whose source is a fixed list of named users is only limited by the technical maximum of 50. Fallback approvers who step in (the flow's fallback list or the default fallback recipients) do not count toward this limit and are likewise only limited by the technical maximum of 50. The total for a stage (its source plus any fallback substitutes, deduplicated) still cannot exceed 50.

maxDueHours.name: Maximum due hours per stage
maxDueHours.help: Lowering it only affects flows added or edited afterwards. Saved flows keep working.

maxCommentLength.name: Maximum length of approval comments
maxCommentLength.help: Lowering it only affects comments submitted afterwards; existing comments are untouched. The most it can be is 1000 characters (the database column length).

maxManagerLevel.name: Maximum manager levels
maxManagerLevel.help: Can be overridden per module, and an override may be wider than the system value. Lowering it only affects flows added or edited afterwards; resolving the manager chain at run time is only limited by the technical maximum of 10 levels.

allowSelfApproval.name: Submitters may approve their own records
allowSelfApproval.help: When on, a submitter who is on a stage approver list or the fallback approver list must approve it personally for the flow to move on. When off, the submitter is always removed from the lists, fallback approvers included. Can be overridden per module.

adminBypassTransitionGroups.name: System administrators can skip the group restriction on status changes
adminBypassTransitionGroups.help: Only covers the group restriction on status changes; the other permissions of system administrators are not affected by this setting.

defaultFallbackApprovers.name: Fallback approvers when no approver is found
defaultFallbackApprovers.help: Used when a flow has no fallback approvers of its own and a stage finds nobody. Choose all system administrators, groups or named users. Only affects tasks created afterwards; existing tasks are unchanged. Can be overridden per module.

alertRecipients.name: Who is notified of approval problems
alertRecipients.help: Who is notified when approval runs into a problem, for example when someone changes the state machine during approval and the transition to take after approval no longer exists. If every listed recipient is disabled or missing, all system administrators are notified instead. Only affects later notifications.

maxAddSignUsers.name: Maximum people per add-sign
maxAddSignUsers.help: How many people one "approve and add signers" action can name. Can be overridden per module. Lowering it only affects later add-signs; stages already added are unchanged. The most it can be is 20.

maxAddSignStages.name: Maximum added stages per record
maxAddSignStages.help: How many added stages one approval of a record can have; an added stage that restarts after a return is not counted again. Can be overridden per module. Lowering it only affects later add-signs. The most it can be is 20.

overdueReminderHours.name: Overdue reminder interval (hours)
overdueReminderHours.help: Once a pending approval is overdue, the assignee gets another overdue reminder when opening notifications only if more than this many hours have passed since the last one. Can be overridden per module. Changing it only affects later reminders. From 1 to 720 hours.

maxWorkflowStates.name: Max workflow states
maxWorkflowStates.help: Checked when saving a workflow or opening an app package; changing other settings of an existing workflow is not affected.

maxWorkflowTransitions.name: Max workflow transitions
maxWorkflowTransitions.help: Checked when saving a workflow or opening an app package; changing other settings of an existing workflow is not affected.

maxRulesPerModule.name: Max field rules per module
maxRulesPerModule.help: Checked when designing rules and when importing or opening a package; existing rules can still be edited.

maxGroupsPerPackage.name: Max groups per package
maxGroupsPerPackage.help: Checked when importing and opening app packages.

maxModulesPerPackage.name: Max modules per package
maxModulesPerPackage.help: Checked when importing and opening app packages.

maxFieldsPerModule.name: Max fields per module in a package
maxFieldsPerModule.help: Checked when importing and opening app packages; adding fields in the designer is not limited by this.

maxOptionsPerField.name: Max options per field in a package
maxOptionsPerField.help: Checked when importing and opening app packages; adding options in the designer is not limited by this.

maxViewsPerModule.name: Max views per module in a package
maxViewsPerModule.help: Checked when importing and opening app packages.

maxIntegrationsPerPackage.name: Max integrations per package
maxIntegrationsPerPackage.help: Checked when importing and opening app packages.

createTitleField.name: Create a "Name" field for new modules
createTitleField.help: When off, a new module only has the "Basic info" block; add fields and choose a title field yourself before activating it.

defaultColumns.name: Columns per row for new blocks
defaultColumns.help: Uses the max columns per row when higher; existing blocks are unchanged.

maxColumns.name: Max columns per row
maxColumns.help: The most columns a block can use; after lowering it, existing blocks keep their columns but cannot be increased.
